q: Explain NAV and units in simple words
expected: A plain explanation that a SIP buys more units when the price is low and fewer when it is high.
answer: A SIP puts the same amount in every month. When the fund price (NAV) is lower you get more units, when it is higher you get fewer. The Gullak value is your units times the latest NAV, so it moves with the market.
